name: TRAVERSE
aliases: Testosterone Replacement Therapy for Assessment of Long-Term Vascular Events and Efficacy Response in Hypogonadal Men
question: Is transdermal testosterone cardiovascularly noninferior to placebo in symptomatic hypogonadal men with established or elevated cardiovascular risk?

design.population: Men aged 45–80 years with hypogonadal symptoms, two fasting testosterone concentrations below 300 ng/dL, and established cardiovascular disease or elevated cardiovascular risk were enrolled at 316 US sites.
design.description: Phase 4, multicenter, double-blind noninferiority randomized trial
design.locator: NEJM pp108–111, Methods and Patients; 5,246 randomization IDs, 5,204 unique participants in full analysis

verdictNote: MACE noninferiority met; pulmonary embolism, atrial fibrillation, and acute kidney injury occurred more often with testosterone.
takeaway: Daily 1.62% testosterone gel was noninferior to placebo gel for cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke over mean 33.0-month follow-up in symptomatic hypogonadal men with established or elevated cardiovascular risk (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.78–1.17).

reports.label: Cardiovascular safety
reports.citation: Lincoff AM, Bhasin S, Flevaris P, et al. "Cardiovascular Safety of Testosterone-Replacement Therapy." *N Engl J Med.* 2023;389(2):107-117. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2215025
reports.followUp: Mean treatment 21.7 months; mean follow-up 33.0 months
reports.followUpLocator: NEJM p107, abstract Results; p111, Patients

results.measure: First cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke
results.note: Prespecified noninferiority margin: upper 95% CI for HR <1.5; safety population received at least one dose.
results.locator: NEJM p114, Table 2; p107, abstract Results

results.measure: First composite cardiovascular event or coronary revascularization
results.note: Secondary analyses were not adjusted for multiplicity.

harms.label: Pulmonary embolism
harms.note: Adjudicated component of venous thromboembolism; no component HR prespecified.

harms.label: Urinary retention (investigator-reported)
harms.note: P=0.08; different ascertainment from adjudicated acute urinary retention in the prostate substudy.

delivery.label: Gel regimen and titration
delivery.value: Daily 1.62% testosterone gel or matching placebo; central algorithm targeted testosterone 350–750 ng/dL, adjusted for hematocrit above 54%.

delivery.label: Analysis populations
delivery.value: 5,246 randomization IDs; 5,204 unique full-analysis participants (2,601 testosterone, 2,603 placebo); 5,198 treated safety participants (2,596 and 2,602).

reports.label: Sexual Function Study
reports.citation: Pencina KM, Travison TG, Cunningham GR, et al. "Effect of Testosterone Replacement Therapy on Sexual Function and Hypogonadal Symptoms in Men with Hypogonadism." *J Clin Endocrinol Metab.* 2024;109(2):569-580. doi:10.1210/clinem/dgad484

results.measure: Between-group mean difference in change in sexual activity, acts per day at 6 months
results.note: Nested Sexual Function Study: 1,161 men with low libido (587 testosterone, 574 placebo).

results.measure: Between-group mean difference in change in sexual activity, acts per day at 12 months
results.note: Treatment effect was maintained at 24 months; arm-specific means unavailable in abstract.

results.endpoint: Sexual desire, symptoms, and erectile function
results.note: Testosterone improved desire and hypogonadal symptoms, but not erectile function; numerical effects unavailable in abstract.

delivery.label: Prostate substudy eligibility
delivery.value: Excluded prior prostate cancer, PSA above 3.0 ng/mL (above 1.5 ng/mL with 5-alpha reductase inhibitor), IPSS above 19, and prostate nodule or induration.

delivery.label: Prostate monitoring
delivery.value: PSA at baseline, 3 months, 12 months, and annually; IPSS at baseline, 3 months, 12 months, 36 months, and study end; digital examination at baseline, 12 months, 36 months, and study end.
delivery.locator: PMC full text, Methods, Assessment of Prostate Safety Events

reports.label: Clinical fractures substudy
reports.citation: Snyder PJ, Bauer DC, Ellenberg SS, et al. "Testosterone Treatment and Fractures in Men with Hypogonadism." *N Engl J Med.* 2024;390(3):203-211. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2308836

results.measure: First adjudicated clinical spine or non-spine fracture, excluding sternum, fingers, toes, facial bones, and skull
results.note: Fracture-reduction hypothesis was not met; fractures were more frequent with testosterone.
